subject: submitButton doesn't seem to control the fileInput module

messages.author: d0def6a2f188e6a9
messages.subject: submitButton doesn't seem to control the fileInput module
parts:
Dear All

I am relatively new to R shiny and recently I've been using it  to create a web app. One issue I encountered is that when I have a series of controls in sidebarPanel (e.g. selectInput, radioButtons, checkboxInput), the submitButton can control all their reactivity except for the fileInput. Consequently, every time I upload the file the figure is generated immediately although I want to hold it until I press the submitButton, can anyone tell me why is this happening?
Below are my ui.R, (I checked the page source and found the  "input type = file " is indeed included in the form)

ui.R
  sidebarPanel(
   
    tags$textarea(id="glist", rows=10, cols=1, "Please input gene list"),
    br(),
    fileInput("gtext", 'Choose gene list file', accept=c('text/plain', '.txt')),
   
    selectInput(inputId = "region", label = "Brain Regions",
      choices = list("ALL" = "ALL", "NCX" = "NCX", "AMY" = "AMY", "STR" = "STR", "URL" = "URL", "DIE" = "DIE", "HIP" = "HIP", "CBC" = "CB"),
                selected = "ALL"),
     
      br(),
      br(),
   
    radioButtons(inputId = "level", label = "Developmental Stages",
                 choices = list("Granular" = "General", "Detailed" = "Detailed"), selected = "Granular"),
     
      br(),
      br(),          
                
                
    checkboxInput("standardize", "Standardize gene profiles", FALSE),
   
      br(),
      br(),
   
      submitButton("Update Figure")
    ),


This is the page source

      <form class="well">
        <textarea id="glist" rows="10" cols="1">Please input gene list</textarea>
        <br/>
        <label>Choose gene list file</label>
        <input id="gtext" type="file" accept="text/plain,.txt"/>
        <div id="gtext_progress" class="progress progress-striped active shiny-file-input-progress">
          <div class="bar"></div>
          <label></label>
        </div>
        <label class="control-label" for="region">Brain Regions</label>
        <select id="region">
          <option value="ALL" selected="selected">ALL</option>
          <option value="NCX">NCX</option>
          <option value="AMY">AMY</option>
          <option value="STR">STR</option>
          <option value="URL">URL</option>
          <option value="DIE">DIE</option>
          <option value="HIP">HIP</option>
          <option value="CB">CBC</option>
        </select>
        <br/>
        <br/>
        <div id="level" class="control-group shiny-input-radiogroup">
          <label class="control-label" for="level">Developmental Stages</label>
          <label class="radio">
            <input type="radio" name="level" id="level1" value="General" checked="checked"/>
            <span>Granular</span>
          </label>
          <label class="radio">
            <input type="radio" name="level" id="level2" value="Detailed"/>
            <span>Detailed</span>
          </label>
        </div>
        <br/>
        <br/>
        <label class="checkbox" for="standardize">
          <input id="standardize" type="checkbox"/>
          <span>Standardize gene profiles</span>
        </label>
        <br/>
        <br/>
        <div>
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Update Figure</button>
        </div>
      </form>


Thanks a lot

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: submitButton doesn't seem to control the fileInput module
parts:
submitButton is very inflexible and fraught with edge cases, and should only be used for the very simplest cases, if at all. actionButton+observe+isolate (soon to be replaced with actionButton+observeEvent) provides a much more flexible and powerful mechanism for accomplishing what submitButton does.

You should be able to accomplish what you want with isolate. Any reactive inputs or expressions you want to access WITHOUT having them trigger reactivity should be put inside isolate (e.g. instead of calling foo() you would do isolate(foo()) ); anything that you do want to trigger reactivity should be outside of isolate.

Thanks Joe !
I've started the transition to actionButton and am pleased to report that it is more straightforward than I had feared.
One hint for people (which is kind of obvious but did still get me). If you have an app with submitButtons in more than one tab and try replacing them one at a time, they won't do what you expect until you have replaced all. Best to comment out all the submitButtons first.
